title: Components of a valid odd split
statement: Let $z$ be a bit string whose odd split parses as a pair encoding. The total first and second projections of that split concatenate to $z$, and the second projected component has length one greater than the first.
hypotheses_covered: The odd split of $z$ parses as a pair encoding
replaced: Let $z$ be a bit string such that $s(z)$ parses as a pair encoding, where $s(z)$ is the odd split of $z$ (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ of the first $i$ bits of $z$ and the rest when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), and $\pi_1, \pi_2$ return the first and second components of a pair encoding (the empty word on strings that do not parse as pairs). Then $z = \pi_1(s(z))\,\pi_2(s(z))$ and $|\pi_2(s(z))| = |\pi_1(s(z))| + 1$.
